model.description: The decision model: `pplx-decider-v1.3` (27B, $0.02 per million input tokens), `pplx-decider-flash-v1.3` (4B, $0.01 per million input tokens), `pplx-decider-v1.2` (27B, $0.02 per million input tokens) or `pplx-decider-flash-v1.2` (4B, $0.01 per million input tokens). The aliases `pplx-decider-latest` and `perplexity/pplx-decider-latest` select `pplx-decider-v1.3`, and `pplx-decider-flash-latest` and `perplexity/pplx-decider-flash-latest` select `pplx-decider-flash-v1.3`; an alias can move to a newer model over time. `pplx-decider-v1-27b` (27B, $0.02 per million input tokens) remains accepted, and `pplx-decider-v1.1-27b` is an alias of it. Images can appear anywhere in `state` as OpenAI-style `image_url` parts with base64 PNG, JPEG, or WebP data URLs and are read in place. Up to 8 images per question. With `mode: "web_grounding"`, a single page URL is fetched and replaced with its text before web search.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Set to `web_grounding` to search the web before the model answers. For a URL-only state, the API first fetches the page and replaces the URL with its text. It then runs one Fast Search per question, up to 100 questions, and adds the top results to `state`. The response lists search evidence in `search_results` and fetched page text in `fetched_results`. If no search returns a result, the model answers from `state`, including any fetched text. Each search costs $0.001 and each successful URL fetch costs $0.0005; fetched text and search evidence count as input tokens. Any other mode value, including an empty string or `null`, returns `400`. See [Web grounding](/docs/decisions/decisions#web-grounding).

The body must stay under 32 MiB.

last_id.description: Opaque cursor for the oldest event in the page, or `null` when `data` is empty. Pass it as `after_id` to fetch the next older page.

LocateQuestion.title: LocateQuestion

type.title: Type
type.description: Always `locate`.

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: What to find in `state`: a short label such as `email address` or an instruction such as `Extract the city where the job is located.` Whitespace-only text returns `400`.
instructions.example: Extract every product name mentioned in the review.

LocateQuestion.description: A question that returns the spans of `state` that match `instructions`. It ignores `criteria` and any other member besides `type` and `instructions`. It needs a v1.3 model: `pplx-decider-v1.3`, `pplx-decider-flash-v1.3`, or the `-latest` aliases that select them; any other model returns `400`. A request with a `locate` question needs a string `state`, no images, and at most 128 questions; with `web_grounding`, a page URL `state` returns `400` with `param` `state`. Other question types can be sent in the same request. Locate was trained on inputs of up to 8k tokens and evaluated on inputs of up to 32k tokens; longer inputs are accepted, but span quality on them is not measured.

start.title: Start
start.description: Offset of the first character of the span in `state`, in Unicode characters.

end.title: End
end.description: Offset after the last character of the span in `state`, in Unicode characters (exclusive).

score.title: Score
score.description: The model's score for the span. Higher means more certainty.

search_result.title: Search Result
search_result.description: With `web_grounding`, present when the span was found in search evidence: the index of that result in `search_results`. `start`, `end`, and `text` then refer to that result's `snippet`.

LocateAnswer.title: LocateAnswer

type.title: Type

spans.title: Spans
spans.description: The spans that match the question, as verbatim substrings of `state`. `[]` when nothing matches.

LocateAnswer.description: Answer to a `locate` question: the matching spans of `state`.

MonitorTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds, for example `2026-11-12T09:00:41Z`.

MonitorStatus.description:
`active` monitors run on their schedule; `paused` ones don't run until
resumed. Whether a run is in flight is `current_run_id`, not the
status. New statuses may be added; treat an unknown one as not
running on its schedule.

MonitorPauseReason.description:
Why a `paused` monitor stopped: you paused it (`user`), credits ran
out, webhook deliveries repeatedly failed (`webhook_failing`), every source the monitor reads repeatedly failed (`source_failing`), or your API Group's policy
no longer allows monitors. Resume it once the cause is
fixed. New reasons may be added; treat an unknown value as a reason to
check the monitor before resuming it.

MonitorFreshness.description: New values may be added; ignore unknown ones in responses.

freshness.description:
Which result date puts a result in the run window: `published`,
`updated`, or both (either date counts). Responses always list
the values in use. `updated` uses the source's last-updated date
with calendar-day precision, not a content-version or page-diff
guarantee. URLs this monitor has already reported stay
suppressed.

include_domains.description: Only results from these domains or their subdomains; `[]` for no restriction

exclude_domains.description: Results from these domains or their subdomains are dropped; may be `[]`

exclude_domains.description:
Up to 20 host names whose results, and their subdomains', are
dropped. A domain may not also be in `include_domains`.

threshold.description: Minimum score, above 0 and up to 1, that every judging check must reach for a result or page change to be kept. A higher value keeps fewer changes.

MonitorJudge.description: Judging settings for this target. Present only when the monitor overrides the default threshold.

threshold.description: Minimum score, above 0 and up to 1, that every judging check must reach for a result or page change to be kept. A higher value keeps fewer changes.

Reports meaningful changes to one URL. The first run of a page
target saves a baseline and reports nothing.

url.description: Absolute `http(s)` URL of a public host, without credentials
Absolute `http(s)` URL of a public host, without credentials

id.description: The profile ID, from 1 to 128 characters.

version.description: The profile version, up to 128 bytes. Omit it to use the latest version.

MonitorAgentTarget.title: Agent target
MonitorAgentTarget.description: An Agent monitor runs the task in `input` on each run. A run with no saved state is a first check. A first check can save at most one update about the current state. Later runs can save up to five updates.

effort.description: The Agent API effort. The service omits this field when the target uses a `profile`.

query.description: Search query to run on each run

max_results.description: Maximum search results considered per query; the run can keep fewer.

input.description: The task for each run, from 1 to 4,000 characters.

effort.description:
Set the effort to one of these values:

- `low`
- `medium`
- `high`

You can add `@latest` or `@<version>` to any value. If you omit `effort` and `profile`, the service uses `low`. Do not send both `effort` and `profile`.

MonitorTargets.description:
Use one of these target configurations:

- One Search target.
- One Agent target.
- One to 10 Page targets with distinct URLs.

Do not mix target types.

interval.description:
A whole number of minutes, hours, days or weeks (`30m`, `6h`,
`1d`, `2w`), from `1m` to `31d`. Responses use the largest exact
unit, so `60m` reads back as `1h`. Runs get up to 10% jitter.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression, for example `0 9 * * 1-5`, without a `TZ=` prefix. Runs may be as often as every minute and at most 31 days apart, checked in `timezone`: monthly passes; quarterly, yearly, the 31st and leap-day schedules are rejected. Runs get up to 10 minutes of jitter.

timezone.description: IANA timezone, for example `Europe/Belgrade`. Optional in requests (default `UTC`); always returned.

MonitorSchedule.description: When a monitor runs. New types may be added.

interval.description:
A whole number of minutes, hours, days or weeks (`30m`, `6h`,
`1d`, `2w`), from `1m` to `31d`. Runs get up to 10% jitter.

MonitorEventType.description: `monitor.changes.detected`: a run succeeded with at least one change. `monitor.run.completed`: a run ended `succeeded` (with or without changes) or `failed`. `monitor.paused`: the service paused the monitor; your own pause sends nothing. `monitor.created`: the first successful run. Subscribe explicitly; it replaces `monitor.changes.detected` and `monitor.run.completed` for that run. New types may be added and are sent only to webhooks that list them in `events`.

MonitorWebhookSecret.description:
Standard Webhooks signing secret: `whsec_` plus the standard (padded)
base64 of 24 to 64 bytes; the HMAC key is the decoded bytes.

url.description: HTTPS endpoint with a public address

events.description:
Event types to send. Omitted or empty means
`[monitor.changes.detected, monitor.paused]`. An unknown type
returns 400 with param `webhook.events[N]`, the index of the
first unknown entry.

secret.description:
Optional signing secret. Without it, create generates one and an
update keeps the current one (or generates one when the monitor
had no webhook). A different secret on update rotates: the old one
also signs for 24 hours. A secret you send is never returned.

events.description: The subscribed event types, defaults filled in

secret.description:
Present only in the response that generated it: a create, or an
update that adds a webhook, without a `secret` in the request.

MonitorMetadata.description: Up to 16 key value pairs; keys 1 to 64 characters, values up to 512 characters (Unicode code points, valid UTF-8). Echoed on every webhook.

CreateMonitorRequest.description: Use a single target type for the monitor. An Agent monitor takes exactly one Agent target.

goal.description: Describe the changes you want the monitor to report. The goal is separate from the Search query or Agent task.

anyOf.description: Optional delivery endpoint; omitted or null sends no events

UpdateMonitorRequest.description: Send only the fields you want to replace. The service keeps the fields you omit. Send `null` to clear `goal`, `metadata`, or `webhook`. When you replace an Agent target, repeat the task and the options you want to keep.

goal.description: Replace the goal without changing the Search query or Agent task. The service returns an empty string after you clear the goal.

anyOf.description:
Replaces the webhook. Without a `secret`, keeps the current one,
or on a monitor without a webhook generates one and returns it in
`webhook.secret` of this response. A new `secret` rotates. `null`
removes the webhook; runs continue and nothing is sent.

MonitorRunStatus.description: `queued` is a manual run that has not started. `skipped` is a run that did not start, including a queued run cancelled by pausing the monitor. New statuses may be added; treat an unknown one as not finished.

Monitor.description:
Fields that do not apply are omitted, never null: `webhook`,
`pause_reason`, `current_run_id`, `next_run_at` and `last_run`.

id.description: Opaque ID with the prefix `mon_`

goal.description: The changes you want the monitor to report. The service returns an empty string if you do not set a goal.

targets.description: The targets for one monitor. An Agent monitor has exactly one target.

has_more.description: Pass the last `data[].id` as `after` for the next page

MonitorRunTrigger.description: What started the run. New triggers may be added; accept unknown values.

MonitorChangeId.description: Stable opaque ID with the prefix `chg_`. Use it to deduplicate the same finding across runs and webhook deliveries.

MonitorSearchResultChange.title: Search result
MonitorSearchResultChange.description: A search result new to the query since the last run

confidence.description: `confidence` is the product of the applicable judging scores, from 0 to 1. The threshold applies to each check, not to the product, so a kept result can have a lower confidence than the threshold. Compare scores within one monitor.

snippet.description: Text from the result, when the source has it

last_updated_at.description: The source's last-updated date, at calendar-day precision, when it has one

MonitorPageChange.title: Page change
MonitorPageChange.description: A meaningful change to a page target

confidence.description: `confidence` is the meaningfulness score, from 0 to 1. The judge uses your goal if you set one.

previous_fetched_at.description: When the earlier of the two compared snapshots was fetched

fetched_at.description: When the later snapshot was fetched

MonitorDiff.description: Text changes between two page checks.

unified.description:
Unified diff without file headers: `@@ -l,s +l,s @@` hunks with one
context line, each line prefixed with ` `, `-` or `+` and ending in
`\n`. Any diff library or viewer reads it. Limited to 24 KiB
(24,576 UTF-8 bytes).

added_lines.description: Added lines in the whole diff, also when `unified` was cut

removed_lines.description: Removed lines in the whole diff, also when `unified` was cut

truncated.description:
Whether `unified` was cut to fit the 24 KiB byte limit. It keeps
complete lines where possible; an oversized line can be shortened
at a UTF-8 character boundary. Its last hunk header counts only
the lines shown.

published_at.description: The publication date of the source, if available.

MonitorAgentUpdateChange.title: Agent update
MonitorAgentUpdateChange.description: An update that the Agent monitor saved.

url.description: The URL of the first source. The service omits this field if `sources` is empty.

title.description: The update title, up to 200 characters.

confidence.description: The confidence score, from 0 to 1. Compare scores within one monitor.

text.description: The text of the update, up to 1,000 characters.

sources.description: Up to five sources for the update. The list can be empty.

MonitorChange.description: A change that the monitor saved. Skip changes with a type you do not recognize.

MonitorPageTargetError.title: Page target error
MonitorPageTargetError.description: A page target that could not be read this run

status_code.description: The page's HTTP status; only with `http_status`

message.description: Human-readable; may change. Do not parse.

MonitorTargetErrorCode.description: Why the page could not be read: the URL is not valid (`invalid_url`), the site blocked the request (`blocked`), the page has no readable text (`no_content`), loading failed (`load_failed`) or timed out (`timeout`), page retrieval is temporarily unavailable (`fetch_unavailable`), or the page returned an error status (`http_status`, with `status_code`). New codes may be added.

MonitorTargetError.description:
A target that could not be read this run; its baseline is kept. New
types may be added; skip errors with an unknown type.

MonitorRunWindow.description: The time range a run covers, `(from, to]`. Before the first successful run, the window starts one schedule period before creation, up to seven days earlier. Later windows normally start where the last successful window ended, subject to the service's lookback limit. The window ends when the run starts.

candidates.description: The number of results, page changes, or Agent updates the monitor considered for this run.

errors.description: Target fetch failures and candidates that could not be judged.

MonitorRunUsage.description: Search and Page runs report nonzero usage only when they succeed. A successful Search run counts as one run for billing. A successful Page run counts each fetched URL that qualifies. An Agent run can report an Agent API cost even if the run fails.

fetched_urls.description: The number of counted URLs that a successful Page run fetched. This value is zero for all other runs.

MonitorRunCost.description: The service estimates the cost at list prices and rounds it to 5 decimal places. This estimate is not the amount charged. A successful Search run costs $0.001 at list prices. A successful Page run costs $0.001 per counted fetched URL at list prices. An Agent run reports only the [Agent API](/docs/getting-started/pricing#agent-api-pricing) cost at list prices, if available.

MonitorRunFailureCode.description: Why a run failed: it could not start (`gate_unavailable`), retrieval failed (`detect_failed`), judging failed (`judge_failed`), every source failed (`source_failed`), the notification could not be scheduled (`notify_failed`), or the run timed out (`timed_out`). New codes may be added; treat an unknown one as a failure to retry on schedule.

MonitorRunError.description:
Why a run failed or was skipped: a `failed` run has `code`, a
`skipped` run has `skip_reason`, the pause reason that refused it.

message.description: Human-readable; may change. Do not parse.

id.description: Opaque ID with the prefix `run_`

has_more.description: Pass the last `data[].id` as `after` for the next page

EventMonitor.description: Enough of the monitor to route an event without a lookup

PausedEventMonitor.description: The paused monitor; `pause_reason` is always set

MonitorEventId.description: Opaque ID with the prefix `evt_`, equal to the `webhook-id` header. The ID stays the same across redeliveries; use it to deduplicate events.

run.description: The run that raised the event, the same object get run returns
The run that caused the pause, when a run caused it

MonitorEvent.description:
A webhook body; `type` says which. Bodies are never truncated: every
change of the run is included. Accept bodies up to 1 MiB. New types
may be added; ignore unknown ones.

MonitorChangesDetectedEvent.title: monitor.changes.detected
MonitorChangesDetectedEvent.description: A run succeeded with at least one change. The first successful run sends `monitor.created` instead.

MonitorRunCompletedEvent.title: monitor.run.completed
MonitorRunCompletedEvent.description: A run ended `succeeded`, with or without changes, or `failed`. The first successful run sends `monitor.created` instead.

MonitorPausedEvent.title: monitor.paused
MonitorPausedEvent.description:
The service paused the monitor (`insufficient_credits`, `org_policy`,
`webhook_failing`, `source_failing`); a pause you make sends nothing.
With reason `webhook_failing` it goes to the failing endpoint, so it
is best-effort.

MonitorCreatedEvent.title: monitor.created
MonitorCreatedEvent.description: The service sends this event only for the first successful run. For Search, `data.run.changes` lists the initial results. Page monitors save a baseline and report no changes. For an Agent monitor, `data.run.changes` can contain one update about the current state. This event replaces `monitor.changes.detected` and `monitor.run.completed` for that run. The default subscription does not include this event.

MonitorWebhookTestEvent.title: monitor.webhook.test
MonitorWebhookTestEvent.description:
Sent only by the test endpoint, never by a subscription; `data` has
no `run`.

MonitorWebhookTest.description: The outcome of one test send

status_code.description: The receiver's HTTP status; omitted when it never answered

duration_ms.description: Time from sending to the answer or the failure

MonitorWebhookTestError.description:
Why the send failed; omitted when delivered. `http_status`: the
receiver answered `status_code` (a 3xx too, since redirects are not
followed). New values may be added.

current_run_id.description: The run already queued or running

MonitorApiErrorType.description:
Machine-readable error type. Monitors returns `invalid_request`
(400), `invalid_api_key`, `token_expired` and
`insufficient_quota` (401), `payment_required` (402),
`forbidden` and `api_product_not_allowed` (403), `not_found`
(404), `invalid_state` (409: the monitor's state does not allow
the request; change it first), `conflict` (409: the monitor was
modified concurrently; retry), `quota_exceeded` (409),
`run_in_progress` (409), `request_rate_limit_exceeded` (429),
`internal_error` (500), `bad_gateway` (502), `service_unavailable` (503) and
`gateway_timeout` (504). New types may be added; act on `code`
for an unknown one.

PromptCacheOptions.title: PromptCacheOptions
PromptCacheOptions.description: Prompt cache options. `implicit` (default) keeps the default cache breakpoints and provider automatic caching. `explicit` turns both off, so only `input_text` parts marked with `prompt_cache_breakpoint` are cached; with no marks, the request makes no cache writes. See [Prompt Caching](/docs/agent-api/prompt-caching).

ttl.description: Accepted for OpenAI compatibility and ignored. Providers apply their default cache lifetime.

PromptCacheBreakpoint.title: PromptCacheBreakpoint
PromptCacheBreakpoint.description: Marks the end of a reusable prompt prefix on an `input_text` part. Marks replace the default cache breakpoints. A request allows up to 4 marks in `explicit` mode and up to 3 in `implicit` mode; more marks, or a mark on another part type, return HTTP 400.

urls.description: 1 to 50 http or https URLs. Your usage tier can lower the maximum. A string that is not an absolute http or https URL does not fail the request: its result has status.type invalid_url.

formats.description: What to return besides metadata, which is always returned for a page with content. highlights requires the highlights object. [] returns metadata only.

if_modified_since.description: A metadata.last_modified value from an earlier response, in IMF-fixdate form such as Thu, 03 Dec 1992 08:37:20 GMT. Requires exactly one URL and max_age_seconds 0. If the page has not changed since then, its result has status.type not_modified and no content, so keep the content you already have.

max_age_seconds.description: Maximum age of a stored copy to accept, up to 63072000 (two years). 0 always fetches the page live. Cannot be combined with snapshot_as_of.

cache_only.description: When true, answer only from stored copies at most max_age_seconds old and never fetch live. A URL without one has status.type no_content. Requires max_age_seconds above 0. Cannot be combined with snapshot_as_of.

snapshot_as_of.description: Return each URL as stored at or before this RFC 3339 time with a time zone, such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z. It must not be in the future or more than 365 days ago. Never fetches live: a URL with no stored copy from before that time has status.type no_content. Cannot be combined with max_age_seconds, cache_only, if_modified_since, or the html and links formats.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget for fetching the pages. URLs are fetched in parallel, and a URL that does not finish in time has status.type crawl_timeout while the rest keep their content. The response can take slightly longer than this budget. With criteria, scoring may add up to 15 seconds.

criteria.description: Decision questions to score each page with, keyed by question ID. 1 to 5 questions. IDs must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, and query is reserved. Scoring never filters, reorders, or drops results.

ContextHighlights.description: Highlights settings. Required when formats includes highlights, and allowed only then.

query.description: What to look for in each page, 1 to 1024 characters. It must contain a non-whitespace character.

max_tokens_per_url.description: Maximum length of each page's highlights, in tokens.

request_id.description: The request ID, the same value as the X-Request-Id response header. Include it when you contact support.

results.description: One result per input URL, in request order.

fetched_urls.description: The number of billed URLs: the results whose status.type is ok or not_modified. Failed URLs are free, so this is 0 when every URL fails.

ContextUsage.description: The number of billed URLs in this request, the criteria scoring tokens when the request has criteria, and the cost at list price.

ContextCost.description: The cost of the request at list price: the per-URL rate for each billed URL, plus the Decisions API input token price of criteria.input_tokens when the request has criteria. It does not reflect account-specific discounts, credits, or adjustments. See [Context API pricing](/docs/getting-started/pricing#context-api-pricing).

total_cost.description: fetched_urls at the list per-URL rate, plus the list price of criteria.input_tokens when the request has criteria, rounded to 5 decimals.

ContextCurrency.description: The currency of total_cost. Always USD.

ContextDocument.description: No field is ever null: a field without a value is omitted. markdown, html, links, and highlights appear only when requested and status.type is ok. metadata appears when status.type is ok or not_modified. A failed result has only url and status.

url.description: The URL exactly as you sent it.

html.description: The page's HTML. Omitted for a page that is not HTML, such as a PDF.

links.description: The page's links resolved to absolute URLs, without duplicates, in page order. [] for a page without links.

highlights.description: The passages of the page most relevant to highlights.query, as one string of extracted page text. Omitted when no passage was returned within max_tokens_per_url.

criteria.description: The answer to each criteria question, keyed by question ID. Only when the request has criteria and status.type is ok; omitted when the page was not scored, and then criteria_error says why if scoring failed.

criteria_error.description: Why scoring failed. Only when the request has criteria, status.type is ok, and criteria is omitted; absent when the page had no text to score. timeout: scoring ran out of time. overloaded: the scoring service was at capacity. error: scoring failed for another reason.

type.description: ok: the fetch succeeded; the result has metadata and the requested formats that are available. not_modified: unchanged since if_modified_since. invalid_url: not an absolute http or https URL. blocked: the URL is blocked and was not fetched. bot_challenge: the site answered with a bot challenge. crawl_failed: the fetch failed. crawl_timeout: fetching the page timed out. no_text: the page has no text, and formats has markdown. no_content: no content was found for the URL. internal_error: the URL could not be read; retry later.

status_code.description: The site's own HTTP status, on ok, not_modified, bot_challenge, and crawl_failed, when the site answered.

message.description: A fixed sentence describing the failure. Only on failures.

ContextMetadata.description: Returned when status.type is ok or not_modified, whatever formats asks for. A field without a value is omitted. Other meta tags in the page's head (name, property, or itemprop) with a non-empty name and value are returned under their lowercased name, such as og:title: a string, or an array of the distinct values in page order when the page repeats the tag.

source_url.description: The URL the content came from, after normalization and redirects. It can differ from url.

origin.description: cached: a stored copy, chosen by max_age_seconds, cache_only, or snapshot_as_of. live: fetched for this request.

fetched_at.description: When the returned content was fetched. Omitted when snapshot_as_of is set.

last_modified.description: The site's Last-Modified header, when it sent one. Send it as if_modified_since to check whether the page changed. It is not a publication date or fetch time.

type.description: The error type. See each status code for its types.

param.description: The request field the error is about, when one applies.

request_id.description: The request ID. Present on errors the Context API returns itself.

instructions.description: The question to answer or the statement to check, 1 to 1000 characters. It must contain a non-whitespace character.

type.description: The question type. Always noul.

criteria.description: Optional descriptions of what makes the answer true and what makes it false.

ContextCriteriaQuestion.description: A yes or no question, or a statement to check, about each page.

true.description: What makes the answer true, 1 to 500 characters. It must contain a non-whitespace character.

false.description: What makes the answer false, 1 to 500 characters. It must contain a non-whitespace character.

ContextCriteriaOutcomes.description: What counts as true and what counts as false.

type.description: Always noul.

noul.description: The probability of yes or true, from 0 to 1. Values near 0.5 mean the model is unsure.

ContextDecisionNoulAnswer.description: The answer to a noul question: the probability that the answer is yes or the statement is true.

ContextCriteriaUsage.description: Token usage for criteria scoring. Present only when the request has criteria and scoring usage was reported.

input_tokens.description: The tokens the decision model read to score the pages (page text plus the questions), billed as Decisions API input tokens.

include_usage.description: When `true`, a final chunk before `data: [DONE]` reports token usage for the whole request.

prompt_tokens.description: Input tokens for the request, including cache reads and writes.

messages.description: The conversation so far, as an array of message objects with `role` and `content`. The leading `system` or `developer` message is applied as the system prompt.

model.description: A model id from the Orchestrator catalog, or `perplexity/auto` to select a model for each request. With Auto, omit `routing` to use the default policy or provide an inline routing object.

reasoning_effort.description: How much reasoning the model performs before answering, on models that support it. Supported values and the default vary by model, and an unsupported value returns a 400.

max_completion_tokens.description: Upper bound on generated tokens for this request, including reasoning tokens. Some Anthropic models with reasoning can report more completion tokens than this value.

response_format.description: Output format. Use type `json_schema` for strict structured output or `json_object` for JSON mode.

stream.description: When `true`, tokens are sent as server-sent events as they are generated, terminated by `data: [DONE]`.

stop.description: One stop string, or an array of at most 4. On models that honor stop sequences, output ends at the first match. Some models accept the field without applying it.

stream_options.description: Streaming options. Only allowed when `stream` is `true`.

tools.description: Function definitions the model can invoke. A tool's `description` is optional.

tool_choice.description: Controls whether the model may call tools, requires a specific tool, or limits selection with `allowed_tools`.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Set to `false` to allow at most one tool call per turn. Defaults to `true`, which allows, but does not require, several calls.

routing.description: Inline routing for `model: "perplexity/auto"` only. Omit this field or set it to null to use the default policy. The serialized routing object must be at most 16384 bytes. Models must be available in the Orchestrator catalog. Routes incompatible with the request are excluded; if the default model is incompatible, the first compatible route model becomes the default. The request fails if no model is compatible.

id.description: Identifier of this completion.
